correctness.rationale: For the exact Aliev tetrahedron Δ, vertex evaluations of integral u=(a,b,c) are 0,(s+a)/2,(s+b)/2,(s+c)/2 with s=a+b+c. Setting x_i=s+u_i is a bijection onto integer triples with sum divisible by four, inverse u_i=x_i-s. Thus twice the lattice width is the integer range of 0,x1,x2,x3. A nonzero u cannot have range <=1: all x_i then lie in {0,1} or {-1,0}; their sum lies between -3,3 and divisible by 4, so all vanish. Range=2 splits exhaustively into (i) nonnegative: permutations of (2,2,0),(2,1,1), (ii) nonpositive negatives, and (iii) mixed: permutations of (-1,0,1). Mapping back gives exactly ±coordinate vectors, six permutations of (1,-1,0), and six mixed-sign ±1 triples, a total of 18 oriented/nine unoriented directions. Determinant of the edge matrix with diagonal 1 off-diagonal 1/2 is 1/2, volume 1/12; width=1 attains known sharp inequality. Independent integer shell enumeration confirmed 18 and independent range check scanned 4,912 nonzero u in [-8,8]^3; universal min lower bound is the congruence proof, not the scan.
residual_risks: Finite independent tests do not certify any unrestricted theorem; analytical argument and published structural lemmas carry generality.
